init.title: Centralite options
init.description: Tune how the integration polls the bridge for state changes.

data_description.poll_interval: Elegance only: how often to send a full ^G query to catch any state drift. Push events are the primary update path; this is a safety net for loads that aren't programmed for spontaneous output. JetStream is push-only and ignores this setting.
data_description.sync_clock_on_connect: When enabled, set the Elegance bridge's real-time clock to Home Assistant's local time after each successful connection (startup and after a reconnect). Corrects clock drift without an automation. Runs only once the link is up, so there's no boot-time race.

organize.title: Move to one device per JetStream unit
organize.description:
Today every light and keypad button sits under one bridge device. This moves each physical JetStream unit onto its own device, so it can have its own name and area.

**What changes**
- {units} devices are created, linked to the bridge.
- {lights} lights move to their device. Their entity IDs, your names, icons and areas are kept.
- {switches} keypad button switches are removed and replaced. Each button gets an event entity ("Button N", for presses at the wall) and a button entity ("Tap button N", to press it from Home Assistant).
- Scenes stay on the bridge.
- Anything that targets the whole bridge device will no longer include the lights.

**Switches that will be removed**
{switch_list}

**Home Assistant automations and scripts that use them or target the bridge**
{references}

This list covers Home Assistant automations and scripts only. It cannot see Node-RED flows, dashboards or templates; check those yourself.

**Lights you renamed**
{renamed}

These keep the name you gave them. To use the device's name instead, turn on "Use device name" in the light's settings afterwards.

This cannot be undone from here. Take a backup first; going back means restoring it.

add_device.title: Add a JetStream device
add_device.description: The device must already be programmed in JetStream Designer, with Send T-Party on and Update Third Party done on the bridge. Adding never changes a device that is already set up; an existing device can only gain buttons.

data_description.device_id: The Device ID shown in JetStream Designer.
data_description.buttons: Required for a keypad. Optional for a dimmer or switch that also has buttons.

add_more.title: Devices to add
add_more.description: {count} device(s) ready to add: {ids}. Nothing is saved until you choose Save.

add_batch.title: Add several JetStream devices
add_batch.description:
One device per line: the Device ID, then dimmer, on/off or keypad, then any button numbers from 1 to 3.

Example:

81, dimmer, 1, 3

82, on/off

90, keypad, 2

v1_migration.title: Centralite v1 entities were migrated
v1_migration.description:
Your previous Centralite integration's entities have been adopted into the new v2 integration:

- {migrated_count} lights/switches/buttons were renamed to the v2 unique_id format (their entity IDs, areas, aliases, icons, and dashboard placements were preserved).
- {deleted_count} entities were removed: old `scene.*` entities (both `-ON` and `-OFF`). In v2 a scene is a single `switch.` entity, a different domain, so the old scene entities can't be reused and are recreated fresh as scene-switches.

**You may need to update automations or dashboards** that referenced the old entity IDs — especially scenes, which move from `scene.turn_on` to a `switch.` entity. Home Assistant does not automatically rewrite YAML automation files.

Migration log:

{summary}

jts_duplicate_ids.title: JetStream import: {count} Device ID(s) used more than once
jts_duplicate_ids.description:
Your JetStream `.jts` file has more than one device with the same Device ID. A Device ID is the address Home Assistant uses to reach a device through the bridge, so only one device per ID could be imported:

{details}

Setup finished and every other device was imported normally.

**To fix it:** in JetStream Designer, give each of these devices its own Device ID and send the change to the device. Then export the `.jts` again, remove this integration entry and add it back with the new file. If the device that was not imported is one you don't need in Home Assistant, you can ignore this notice.

jetstream_layout_deprecated.title: {title}: move to one device per JetStream unit
jetstream_layout_deprecated.description:
This JetStream bridge still shows every light and keypad button under a single device. A newer layout gives each physical unit its own device, and replaces the keypad button switches with event and button entities.

Nothing changes until you choose to move: go to **Settings > Devices & services > Centralite > Configure > Move to one device per JetStream unit**. That screen lists exactly what will change, including the button switches that will be removed.

In version 4.0, bridges that have not moved will be moved automatically. If you use the button switches in automations or Node-RED flows, move when you are ready to update them.
